title: Two-pass scan machine
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a symbol alphabet, $A$ a state type, $k$ a natural number, and $i$ one of the $k$ work tapes. Given forward and backward transition functions $\delta_f,\delta_b:A\times\Gamma\to A\times\Gamma$ and an initial state $a_0$, define a machine that starts in the forward phase carrying $a_0$. On each nonblank symbol of tape $i$, the forward phase applies $\delta_f$, writes its output symbol on that tape, moves right, and carries the new state. At a blank it moves left into the backward phase, carrying the current state. The backward phase applies $\delta_b$ to each nonblank symbol, writes the resulting symbol, moves left, and carries the new state; at a blank it moves right into the done phase. In the done phase it stays in place. The input head does not move, and no output symbols are emitted.
hypotheses_covered: A natural number $k$ of work tapes
A selected tape $i$ among the $k$ work tapes
Forward and backward transition functions $A\times\Gamma\to A\times\Gamma$
